svg.title: Amazon S3
svg.desc: Amazon S3. Object storage: objects in buckets, addressed by key, stored across Availability Zones, with storage classes, versioning and events. Step 1, Where it sits: S3 is the app's file store: phones upload with presigned URLs, CloudFront serves, events start work. Step 2, Put an object: Signature and expiry checked, bytes stored redundantly across AZs, then 200 OK; a GET sees it. Step 3, Versions and lifecycle: A second PUT adds version 2; a DELETE adds a delete marker. A lifecycle rule moves originals colder. Step 4, Events, access, limits: Event → SQS → thumbnail. An unsigned GET gets 403; CloudFront reads via OAC. Mind the limits.

g.text: S3 is the app's file store: phones upload with presigned URLs, CloudFront serves, events start work.
Signature and expiry checked, bytes stored redundantly across AZs, then 200 OK; a GET sees it.
A second PUT adds version 2; a DELETE adds a delete marker. A lifecycle rule moves originals colder.
Event → SQS → thumbnail. An unsigned GET gets 403; CloudFront reads via OAC. Mind the limits.
200 OK ETag "9b2cf535…" only after the bytes are stored
GET right after → the new photo (strong read-after-write)
filter prefix u/: thumbnails/ won't loop
The API signs a 15-minute upload URL and never handles the bytes
The phone PUTs IMG_0042.jpg straight into the bucket
CloudFront serves the thumbnails; Athena queries objects in place
A bucket lives in one Region; bucket names share a global namespace
An object is a key, its bytes, metadata and a version ID: 0 B to 50 TB
No limit on the number of objects or bytes in a bucket
S3 recomputes the SigV4 signature and checks the expiry time
It stores the bytes redundantly across ≥ 3 AZs, then answers 200 OK
A GET or LIST right after sees the new photo: strong consistency
u/9f3c/IMG_0042.jpg is one key in a flat namespace: no folders
u/ and u/9f3c/ are prefixes that LIST, rules and limits use
From 100 MB, upload in parts: 5 MiB to 5 GiB each, ≤ 10,000 parts
One PUT ≤ 5 GB; one object ≤ 50 TB (since December 2025)
A PUT to an existing key adds a version; nothing is overwritten
DELETE adds a delete marker, so a plain GET returns 404
Undo: delete the marker; every version stays readable by versionId
Each version is a whole object, stored and billed in full
LIFECYCLE ON u/ · PRICE PER GB-MONTH, US-EAST-1
Old versions expire 30 days after they stop being current
New buckets: Block Public Access on, ACLs off, SSE-S3 encryption
Unsigned GET of the object URL → 403 AccessDenied
Bucket policy: only this CloudFront distribution may GetObject
IAM: API writes u/*; Thumbnailer reads u/* and writes thumbnails/*
≥ 3,500 writes and 5,500 reads per second per prefix
No edits in place: a change is a new PUT of the whole object
Events arrive at least once, unordered, usually within seconds
You pay for GB-months, requests, retrievals and data out
